title: Subprocessor Onboarding & Scoped Access — Negotiation Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This working playbook is intended for negotiators (legal, security, and vendor ops) to use when evaluating and contracting subprocessors who will process Redwood customer data or have access to production environments. It focuses on scoped access, minimal privilege, monitoring obligations, and contractual fallbacks. Not a finalized template — operational guidance + recommended clause text + a practical checklist for triage and negotiation.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Aim to limit subprocessor access to the narrowest scope required, codify accountabilities, and ensure observable controls with defined remediation and exit mechanics.

Negotiation principles (priority order):
1) Minimize access surface (technical and administrative).
2) Require logging + log retention + tamper-evident storage for access to customer data.
3) Require documented subprocessors and restrict further subcontracting without consent.
4) Define incident handling, breach notification SLAs, and proof-of-remediation obligations.
5) Ensure data return/deletion and transitional support on contract termination.
6) Preserve Redwood rights to audit (remote + on-site where feasible) and receive evidence of control effectiveness.

Risk tiering (recommended):
- Tier 1 (High): Subprocessors with access to unredacted customer data, secret keys, or production KVs. Require strict contractual controls, encryption-at-rest/transport, and onboarding SRE reviews.
- Tier 2 (Medium): Subprocessors processing pseudonymized or derived data, or who can trigger production workflows (but not read raw PII). Require SOC2 or equivalent, targeted access controls.
- Tier 3 (Low): Non-sensitive vendors (marketing platforms, analytics) — standard DPA language ok, but scoped access still recommended.

Key contract clauses (recommended language snippets and negotiation notes):
1) Scoped Access / Principle of Least Privilege:
- Recommended clause text: "Subprocessor shall only access Customer Data strictly as necessary to perform the Services, and only to the extent described in Schedule A (Authorized Data & Purpose). Access must be role-based, time-limited, and auditable."
- Negotiation notes: Ask for concrete role names and minimum permissions (e.g., read-only S3 bucket xyz-prod for 72 hours) rather than broad phrases like "as needed." If vendor resists, require post-hoc approval workflow + documented justification for any elevated access.

2) Sub-subcontracting / Transparency:
- Text: "Subprocessor will not engage subprocessors without providing Redwood with a list at least 15 business days in advance and obtaining written consent for Tier 1 subprocessors. Redwood may withhold consent for reasonable security or compliance reasons."
- Notes: For large managed-service vendors, expect pushback on 15-day notice. Acceptable compromise: regular roster updates + right to object within 10 business days for Tier 1.

3) Logging, Monitoring, and Evidence:
- Text: "For any access to Customer Data, Subprocessor will maintain immutable access logs for a minimum of 12 months (or longer if required by law), provide log exports within 3 business days upon reasonable request, and detect anomalous access with defined alerting."
- Notes: If vendor uses a SaaS management layer that aggregates logs, require tamper-evident storage (WORM) or a signed hash chain for logs.

4) Incident Notification and Forensic Support:
- Text: "Subprocessor will notify Redwood within 24 hours of detection of any security incident affecting Customer Data, provide a root-cause analysis within 10 business days, and support remediation activities including log exports, preservation of forensic evidence, and stabilization steps."
- Notes: 24-hour detection notification is a hard ask for Tier 1. If vendor asks for 72 hours, require compensating controls (e.g., monitoring proof, IR runbooks, SOC escalation policy).

5) Data Return, Deletion, and Transition Support:
- Text: "Upon termination or expiration, Subprocessor will, at Redwood’s election, securely return or delete Customer Data within 30 days and provide written certification. Where deletion is infeasible, subprocessor will isolate data and ensure continuing compliance until destroyed."
- Notes: For vendors that backup data across multiple systems, require a deletion map and schedule with attestations over a 90-day window.

6) Audit Rights and Control Evidence:
- Text: "Redwood has the right to conduct (i) remote control testing and (ii) one onsite audit per 12 months for Tier 1 subprocessors, or to receive equivalent third-party audit reports and evidence (SOC2 Type II or ISO27001 audit scope that maps to services)."
- Notes: Vendors may prefer producing SOC2 reports. If they do, require management assertions linking controls to production systems that handle Redwood data and an opportunity to submit targeted follow-up questions.

7) Encryption and Key Management:
- Text: "Subprocessor will encrypt Customer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard algorithms. For Tier 1, cryptographic keys will be customer-dedicated (or Redwood-provided) where technically possible. Key rotation policies and KMS access lists must be provided on request."
- Notes: True customer-managed keys are often a dealbreaker for small vendors; accept HSM-backed vendor-managed KMS only for Tier 2/3 with strong attestation and restricted personnel access.

8) Liability and Remedies (practical asks):
- Text: "Subprocessor’s liability for breaches of Customer Data or gross negligence shall be uncapped for direct damages and include indemnity for regulatory fines arising from Subprocessor’s acts or omissions."
- Notes: Vendors will resist uncapped liability. Reasonable compromise: carve-outs for inadvertent errors, insurance-backed caps (minimum $5M cyber), and contractual indemnity for regulatory penalties caused by vendor negligence. Document negotiation path in the contract file.

Operational checklist (To be completed by vendor-ops / security reviewer pre-sign):
- Does the contract identify specific systems / buckets / databases and the purpose for access? (Yes/No)
- Are access roles and justifications documented? (Yes/No + link to access request ticket)
- Is there a subprocessor roster and approval workflow? (Yes/No)
- Are logging retention, format, and export SLAs defined? (Yes/No)
- Incident notification SLA specified (hours) and forensic support defined? (Yes/No)
- Encryption at rest and in transit confirmed? (Yes/No)
- Key management approach described (vendor-managed / customer-managed)? (Notes)
- Audit evidence provided (SOC2/ISO) and scope mapped? (Yes/No + attach)
- Cyber insurance minimum coverage documented? (Yes/No)
- Exit and deletion plan attached? (Yes/No + windows)

Playbook: sample negotiation paths and redlines (practical examples)
- Vendor: "We maintain logs for 90 days only."
  Redwood ask: 12 months for Tier 1 or a compromise of 6 months + ability to pull archived logs on request.

- Vendor: "No onsite audits. Provide SOC2 instead."
  Redwood ask: Accept SOC2 Type II if the scope includes the services and has bridging controls. Add a clause for targeted control testing or an on-demand review if anomalies are found.

- Vendor: "Subcontracting allowed without notice."
  Redwood ask: Advance notice for Tier 1 and right to object. If vendor refuses, require that any new subprocessors inherit the same contractual obligations and allow Redwood to terminate services on reasonable notice.

Decision thresholds for escalation (when to involve Legal Lead / CISO / Exec):
- Involve Legal Lead: Vendor refuses to provide retention or incident notification windows for Tier 1.
- Involve CISO: Vendor cannot demonstrate encryption-at-rest or claims no centralized logging for production systems.
- Involve Exec: Vendor refuses any liability exposure or denies audit rights for systems that process customer data.

Template attachments (placeholders — link to versions in Confluence):
- Schedule A: Authorized Data & Purpose (fill with explicit resource names)
- Schedule B: Access Roles Matrix (role, scope, duration, justification)
- Exhibit 1: Incident Response Checklist + Evidence Request List

Next steps for reviewers (quick action items):
- Security reviewer: populate the Operational checklist and confirm Tier classification. Link the completed checklist to JIRA-SEC-781.
- Legal negotiator: propose the redlines in vendor contract, annotate with negotiation notes above. Use CLA/negotiation channel #vendor-legal on Slack for quick triage.
- Vendor Ops: if Tier 1, schedule onboarding runbook with SRE and require one-week shadow access window before any elevated access.

Notes / unresolved questions (working):
- For vendors using third-party cloud logging (e.g., vendor-managed Splunk), we need a standard attestation template for log integrity — unfinalized.
- How strict should the deletion attestation be when backups span multiple legal jurisdictions? Suggest involving privacy counsel for cross-border retention mapping.

Revision history:
- v0.1 (2024-09-18) initial draft — Aisha
- v0.2 (2024-11-02) added decision thresholds and practical redline examples — Lina

End of doc.
